concepts.statement: WACC weights each source of finance by its market value, not its book value, and uses debt's after-tax cost, not its quoted rate — the tax shield on interest is part of what debt actually costs the firm. Book-value weights or a pre-tax cost of debt both misstate the discount rate applied to project cash flows.

concepts.subsection: Advanced Capital Budgeting Decisions — real options
concepts.statement: A project's strategic value is its static NPV plus the value of the flexibility attached to it — options to expand, abandon or delay that ordinary discounting prices at zero. A negative static NPV can still be worth taking up when the option it carries is worth more than the shortfall.

concepts.subsection: Risk in capital budgeting — sensitivity, scenario and simulation
concepts.statement: Sensitivity analysis moves one variable at a time to find each one's break-even point. Scenario analysis moves several variables together in a few named, internally consistent bundles — best, base, worst. Simulation draws thousands of random combinations from each variable's probability distribution and builds the full outcome distribution, which the other two only sample at a handful of points.

A one-step binomial model prices an option from the two possible next-period stock prices using the risk-neutral probability that makes the stock's own expected return equal the risk-free rate — not the real-world probability of an up move, which plays no part in a no-arbitrage price. The expected payoff under that probability is then discounted at the risk-free rate.

concepts.subsection: Derivatives Analysis and Valuation — Black-Scholes inputs
concepts.statement: Black-Scholes prices an option from five inputs: spot, strike, time to expiry, the risk-free rate and volatility. A call rises with spot, time, the rate and volatility, and falls with a higher strike; volatility raises both the call and the put together, since either option gains from a larger move and loses no more than its premium either way.

Duration prices the bond's yield sensitivity as a straight line; convexity is the curvature that line misses. Because the true price-yield curve bends away from the line, a positive-convexity bond gains more from a yield fall than duration predicts and loses less from an equal yield rise — the convexity term always adds back value that a duration-only estimate leaves out.

Current yield is the annual coupon divided by the bond's market price, not its face value. For a bond trading below par, the order runs coupon rate < current yield < yield to maturity, because YTM also captures the pull to par at redemption that current yield ignores; above par the order reverses, and only a par bond has all three equal.

A credit default swap transfers a bond's default risk from a protection buyer to a protection seller: the buyer pays a periodic spread regardless of what happens, and the seller pays out only if the reference entity defaults, and then only the loss given default — the face value less whatever the recovery rate returns.

The theoretical ex-rights price weights the cum-rights price and the subscription price by the number of old and new shares, not by a simple average of the two prices. The value of the right attached to one existing share is the ex-rights price less the subscription price, divided by the number of old shares needed to subscribe for one new share.

Walter's model prices a share as P = [D + (r/Ke)(E − D)] / Ke and ties the optimal payout to how the firm's internal return r compares with its cost of equity Ke — retain everything when r exceeds Ke, since the firm compounds cash better than the market prices it; pay out everything when r is below Ke; payout is irrelevant only at r = Ke, the special case MM's irrelevance proposition generalises.

concepts.subsection: Mergers, Acquisitions and Corporate Restructuring — leveraged buyouts
concepts.statement: A leveraged buyout funds most of the purchase price with debt secured on the target's own assets and cash flows, leaving the sponsor's equity a small slice of the deal. Returns come from paying that debt down over the holding period — and from any exit-multiple expansion — so the same flat operating performance produces a far larger percentage return on the sponsor's equity than on the deal as a whole.

citation.ref: Ch. Mergers, Acquisitions and Corporate Restructuring

concepts.subsection: Portfolio Management — two-asset risk and correlation
concepts.statement: A two-asset portfolio's standard deviation equals the weighted average of the two assets' standard deviations only when they are perfectly positively correlated. At any lower correlation the covariance term in the variance formula is smaller than that limiting case, and the portfolio's risk falls below the weighted average — the diversification benefit correlation below one always buys.

Diversification removes unsystematic risk, the part specific to individual securities. What remains in a well-diversified portfolio is systematic risk, which beta measures and which no amount of diversification can remove.
An option premium is intrinsic value plus time value. A put's intrinsic value is the excess of strike over spot (zero if spot is higher); whatever of the premium is not intrinsic value is time value.

concepts.subsection: Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management
concepts.statement: Under interest rate parity, the currency with the higher interest rate trades at a forward discount and the lower-rate currency at a forward premium, by the interest differential — otherwise borrowing in one currency and depositing in the other would be a free profit.

citation.ref: Ch. Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management

concepts.statement: Duration measures a bond's price sensitivity to interest rate changes. It rises with maturity and falls with coupon; a zero-coupon bond's duration equals its maturity, the maximum for any bond of that term.

To hedge a stock portfolio with index futures, the number of contracts is the portfolio's value multiplied by its beta, divided by the value of one futures contract. Ignoring beta hedges a different portfolio than the one held.

concepts.subsection: Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management
concepts.statement: An importer with a foreign currency payable loses when that currency rises, so the hedge is to buy it forward or buy a call option on it. A forward locks the rate both ways; the option caps the cost while keeping the gain if the currency falls, at the price of the premium.

citation.ref: Ch. Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management

concepts.statement: When mutually exclusive projects rank differently under NPV and IRR, NPV decides. IRR assumes reinvestment at the IRR itself and can prefer a small project with a high rate over a large one that adds more value; NPV measures the wealth actually added at the real cost of capital.

Net asset value per unit is the market value of the fund's investments plus other assets, minus liabilities and accrued expenses, divided by units outstanding. Entry and exit prices derive from NAV, and the expense ratio quietly drags it every day.

Under constant dividend growth, equity value per share is next year's expected dividend divided by the excess of the required return over the growth rate. The model runs on the coming dividend, not the one just paid, and dies where growth meets or beats the required return.

A forward rate agreement fixes today the interest rate for a future borrowing or deposit period — a 6x9 FRA covers a three-month period starting six months out. The buyer gains when rates rise above the agreed rate and is compensated by a discounted settlement at the period's start; no principal ever moves.

For European options on the same share, strike and expiry, the call price minus the put price equals the share price minus the present value of the strike. When market prices break that chain, a riskless arbitrage exists — buy the cheap side, sell the dear one, and lock the difference.

Sharpe divides excess return by total risk (standard deviation); Treynor divides the same excess return by systematic risk (beta). For a fully diversified portfolio the two rank alike, because diversification has squeezed out the unsystematic part. Where they disagree, the fund is carrying diversifiable risk the market does not pay for.

concepts.subsection: CAPM and the security market line
concepts.statement: CAPM's required return is the risk-free rate plus beta times the market risk premium. A security whose expected return sits above that line has positive alpha — it is underpriced, and the decision rule says buy; below the line, overpriced, sell. Alpha measures mispricing against systematic risk only.

The fair futures price is the spot price grown at the carrying cost — financing, storage, minus any yield the asset throws off. A traded futures price above fair value invites cash-and-carry arbitrage (buy spot, sell futures); below fair value, reverse cash-and-carry (sell spot, buy futures). The arbitrage, not opinion, is what pins the price to the formula.

In a share-for-share merger, the acquirer's EPS rises when the price paid values the target at a lower price-earnings multiple than the acquirer's own, and falls when the target is bought at a higher multiple. The exchange ratio decides how the combined earnings spread over the combined shares; accretion is arithmetic, not evidence of a good deal.

citation.ref: Ch. Mergers, Acquisitions and Corporate Restructuring

concepts.statement: A money market hedge manufactures a forward rate from the two interest rates: an exporter awaiting foreign currency borrows that currency today against the receivable, converts at spot, and invests at home; the foreign loan is repaid by the receivable itself. If interest rate parity holds exactly, the locked-in rate equals the forward rate and the choice is a matter of transaction cost and access, not principle.

citation.ref: Ch. Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management

concepts.statement: Value at Risk states the largest loss expected over a stated horizon at a stated confidence — a one-day 99 per cent VaR of ₹10 lakh means one trading day in a hundred should lose more than ₹10 lakh. It says nothing about how much worse that hundredth day gets, which is the measure's famous blind spot.

concepts.subsection: Capital market line and security market line
concepts.statement: The capital market line prices total risk (standard deviation) and holds only efficient portfolios — combinations of the risk-free asset and the market portfolio. The security market line prices systematic risk (beta) and holds every fairly priced asset, efficient or not. A single stock full of diversifiable risk plots on the SML yet below the CML.

Modigliani and Miller hold that in a perfect market — no taxes, no transaction costs, no information gaps — dividend policy cannot change shareholder wealth: paying a dividend drops the ex-dividend price by the same amount, and a shareholder wanting cash can manufacture a dividend by selling shares. Real-world relevance arguments live exactly in the frictions the proof assumes away — taxes, signalling, clientele effects.

In a plain vanilla interest rate swap one party pays fixed and receives floating on a notional principal that is never exchanged; only net interest differences change hands each period. A borrower with floating-rate debt who pays fixed on a swap has synthetically fixed its cost; the swap's value at inception is zero and moves as rates move.

concepts.subsection: Foreign exchange — cross rates and triangular arbitrage
concepts.statement: Three currencies imply each cross rate from the other two; when a quoted cross rate strays from the implied rate, riding the three legs in the right circle returns more of the starting currency than was put in, risk-free. The direction matters — one way round the triangle profits, the other way loses — and the trade itself pushes the quotes back into line.

citation.ref: Ch. Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management

concepts.statement: Free cash flow to the firm belongs to all capital providers and discounts at the weighted average cost of capital to give enterprise value; free cash flow to equity — FCFF less after-tax interest and net debt repayments — belongs to shareholders alone and discounts at the cost of equity to give equity value directly. Mixing a flow with the other side's discount rate is the classic valuation error.

concepts.subsection: Risk in capital budgeting — certainty equivalents
concepts.statement: The certainty equivalent approach shrinks each risky cash flow to the certain amount the decision-maker would accept instead, then discounts at the risk-free rate; the risk-adjusted discount rate approach keeps the expected flows and loads the risk into a higher rate. The rate route compounds the risk penalty with time even when risk does not grow; certainty equivalents price each year's risk on its own.

A foreign project can be valued two ways that must agree: discount foreign currency cash flows at the foreign discount rate and convert the NPV at spot, or convert each year's flows at expected forward rates and discount in home currency at the home rate. Mixing — foreign flows with the home rate, or forwards with the foreign rate — builds the currency premium in twice or not at all.

A bond portfolio is immunised against interest rate moves by matching its duration to the investment horizon: a rate rise then costs price but earns more on reinvested coupons, a fall does the reverse, and at the horizon the two effects offset. The match decays as time passes and rates move — durations drift at different speeds — so immunisation needs periodic rebalancing, not a one-time set-up.

concepts.subsection: Option strategies — protective put and covered call
concepts.statement: A protective put — stock plus a bought put — buys insurance: losses stop at the strike, the upside stays open, and the premium is the cost of certainty. A covered call — stock plus a sold call — sells the upside: the premium is income, gains cap at the strike, and the downside stays open less the premium. One pays to remove tail risk; the other is paid to surrender tail gain.

A currency swap exchanges principal and interest in one currency for principal and interest in another — and unlike an interest rate swap, the principals are real: exchanged at the start (or notionally referenced) and re-exchanged at maturity at the original rate, which is where the currency risk transfers. Each party ends up servicing debt in the currency it wanted, typically borrowing where it borrows cheapest first and swapping.

citation.ref: Ch. Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management

concepts.statement: APT prices assets from several systematic factors — industrial production, inflation surprises, interest rates, credit spreads — each with its own beta and premium, where CAPM compresses all systematic risk into one market beta. APT's discipline is arbitrage: two portfolios with identical factor exposures must earn identical expected returns, or the difference is picked up risk-free. It says nothing about which factors — that is empirical.

Lease-or-buy is a financing comparison, so its cash flows — lease rentals net of tax shield, forgone depreciation shields, salvage forgone — discount at the after-tax cost of debt, not the project's cost of capital: the lease displaces borrowing of equivalent risk. The investment decision comes first and separately; a bad project is not rescued by a clever lease.

Securitisation sells a pool of receivables to a bankruptcy-remote special purpose vehicle that funds the purchase by issuing securities serviced by the pool's collections. True sale takes the assets off the originator's balance sheet; tranching splits the paper into senior, mezzanine and equity slices absorbing losses bottom-up; credit enhancement — overcollateralisation, subordination, guarantees — lifts the senior tranche's rating above the originator's own.

Startup money arrives in stages priced to risk: bootstrapping and friends-and-family at the idea, angels at the prototype, venture capital in lettered rounds as revenue proves out, and strategic or public markets at maturity. Each round prices the company anew — pre-money plus new cash equals post-money — and earlier holders dilute unless they follow on. Venture investors buy convertible preferred with liquidation preference, anti-dilution and board rights, not plain equity.

Transaction exposure is a booked receivable or payable awaiting settlement — hedgeable with forwards and options. Translation exposure is the accounting restatement of foreign subsidiaries' balances at consolidation — a reporting effect with no cash flow of its own. Economic exposure is the deepest: the effect of exchange rates on future competitiveness and cash flows, reaching even firms that never invoice abroad, and managed by operational choices more than by derivatives.

citation.ref: Ch. Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management

concepts.subsection: Mutual funds — costs and tracking error
concepts.statement: The expense ratio is deducted from the fund's assets daily, so investors earn the portfolio's return minus costs — a one-and-a-half per cent ratio on an eight per cent market compounds into a fifth of the wealth over decades. For index funds the second report card is tracking error: the volatility of the fund's return differences against its benchmark. Low fees with faithful tracking is the entire proposition of passive investing.

concepts.subsection: Futures — margins and marking to market
concepts.statement: A futures position opens with initial margin and is marked to market daily — losses are debited and gains credited to the margin account each evening at the settlement price. When the balance falls below the maintenance margin, a margin call demands topping back up to the initial level; failure triggers position closure. Daily settlement is why futures carry negligible counterparty risk and why they can bankrupt a trader long before expiry.

concepts.subsection: Interest rate caps, floors and collars
concepts.statement: A cap pays the borrower whenever the reference rate fixes above the strike — insurance against rising rates, bought for a premium; a floor pays the lender when rates fix below its strike. A borrower's collar buys a cap and sells a floor, financing the protection by surrendering the benefit of falls below the floor — at zero net cost when the strikes are chosen so the premiums offset. The borrower's rate then lives inside a band.

EVA charges profit for all the capital that earned it: net operating profit after tax minus the capital employed times its weighted average cost. A company can grow accounting profit every year while destroying value, if the new profit earns less than the capital's cost. Positive EVA — return on capital above WACC — is what accounting profit alone never certifies.

A term loan turns non-performing when interest or principal stays overdue for more than ninety days; a cash credit when the account stays out of order. Once non-performing, the asset walks a ladder — substandard for its first twelve months as an NPA, doubtful once it stays substandard beyond twelve months, loss when identified as such — and income on it is recognised only on realisation, not accrual.

citation.ref: Prudential norms on Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning

concepts.statement: The LFAR is the RBI-prescribed questionnaire the bank auditor answers alongside the main report — advances, credit appraisal, NPA identification, internal controls, frauds — branch LFARs feeding the central auditor's consolidated one. It supplements the statutory report and does not dilute it: a matter grave enough to affect the true and fair view belongs in the main report, qualified, not parked in the LFAR.

Section 141(3)(d) with Rule 10 draws money lines around the auditor's independence: a relative may hold securities of the company up to one lakh rupees face value; indebtedness to the company beyond five lakh rupees disqualifies; a guarantee for a third party's debt to the company beyond one lakh rupees disqualifies. The disqualification reaches the member, the firm and its partners, and one incurred during the term vacates the office.

CARO's fraud clause asks three things: whether any fraud by the company or on the company was noticed or reported during the year, with nature and amount; whether any section 143(12) report was filed in Form ADT-4; and whether the auditor considered whistle-blower complaints received by the company. The clause covers fraud on the company by anyone, not only by its officers and employees.

SQC 1 requires an engagement quality control review — an objective evaluation of the significant judgments and the conclusions reached — for audits of financial statements of listed entities, completed before the report is dated. The reviewer stands outside the engagement team, and the report cannot be signed past an unresolved difference with the reviewer.

An audit expresses an opinion on financial statements against a framework; due diligence is a purchaser-side examination of a target's whole position — financial, legal, operational — to price a deal and surface hidden liabilities; an investigation is a deep, targeted probe into a suspected specific matter, going wherever the suspicion leads. Scope, purpose and the reporting audience differ across all three; assurance levels are not interchangeable.

citation.ref: Ch. Due Diligence, Investigation and Forensic Accounting

concepts.statement: Propriety audit asks questions regularity audit cannot: not only was the expenditure sanctioned and lawful, but was it wise, economical, and free of personal advantage — would a person of ordinary prudence have spent his own money so? The C&AG's audit of public undertakings runs on both rails, and a transaction can pass every rule yet fail propriety.

citation.ref: Ch. Audit of Public Sector Undertakings

concepts.statement: Peer review examines a practice unit's systems — whether its quality controls, documentation and compliance with technical standards for attestation services are adequate and were followed — through sample engagements. The reviewer evaluates the unit, not the clients: a review is not a second audit of any auditee, and its report speaks to the unit's systems, leading to a peer review certificate.

A company's first auditor (other than a government company) is appointed by the board within thirty days of registration; if the board fails, the members appoint within ninety days at an extraordinary general meeting. The first auditor holds office until the conclusion of the first annual general meeting — and needs no ratification meanwhile.

Forensic engagements run under ICAI's Forensic Accounting and Investigation Standards and differ from audit at the root: the mindset presumes the possibility of fraud rather than neutrality, procedures chase evidence that will stand in legal proceedings — chain of custody, corroboration, documentation to litigation grade — and the outcome states findings of fact, not an opinion or an assurance conclusion. Materiality thresholds do not excuse small frauds from a forensic scope.

citation.ref: Ch. Due Diligence, Investigation and Forensic Accounting

concepts.statement: RBI regulates NBFCs in layers by size and risk — base, middle, upper and a normally empty top layer — with regulatory intensity rising through the stack: the upper layer carries bank-like requirements. The auditor's concerns scale accordingly: income recognition and asset classification norms, the layer's specific prudential requirements, and the statutory auditor's own direct reporting duties to RBI on matters such as non-compliance with the RBI Act.

citation.ref: Ch. Audit of Non-Banking Financial Companies

concepts.statement: Section 143(3) prescribes what every company audit report states: whether information and explanations sought were obtained, whether proper books were kept, whether the accounts agree with the books, whether the statements comply with the accounting standards, the section 164(2) director disqualification status, internal financial controls where applicable, and the rule-prescribed matters. Each is answered — a negative or qualified answer comes with reasons under 143(4).

General IT controls govern the environment — access, change management, operations, backup — while application controls live inside each system, checking individual transactions: input validations, exception reports, interface reconciliations. Weak general controls undermine every application control running on that system, so the auditor tests the foundation before relying on what stands on it; automated controls tested once can be relied on across the period only if change management held.

citation.ref: Ch. Audit in an Automated Environment

concepts.subsection: Section 144 — Services an auditor may not render
concepts.statement: A company's auditor may not render, directly or indirectly, to the company, its holding or its subsidiary: accounting and book keeping, internal audit, design and implementation of financial information systems, actuarial services, investment advisory and investment banking, outsourced financial services, and management services. "Directly or indirectly" reaches the auditor's relatives, connected persons and entities using the firm's brand or network. Permitted other services need audit committee or board approval.

In a general insurer's audit the claims liability has two layers: outstanding claims — reported but unsettled, verified against surveyor reports and case estimates — and claims incurred but not reported (IBNR), an actuarial estimate the appointed actuary certifies and the auditor evaluates as an accounting estimate using an expert's work. Premium deficiency and unexpired risk reserves sit beside them; the auditor tests data integrity feeding the actuary as hard as the outputs.

A review gives limited assurance in negative form — "nothing has come to our attention" — built mainly on inquiry and analytical procedures; an agreed-upon procedures engagement gives no assurance at all, reporting factual findings of the exact procedures the parties specified, for those parties alone to judge. An audit's reasonable assurance sits above both. Naming the engagement wrongly misleads every reader about what stands behind the numbers.

citation.ref: Ch. Review and Related Services (SRE 2400, SRS 4400)

concepts.subsection: First Schedule Part II — Members in service
concepts.statement: A member in employment commits professional misconduct by paying any person a share of the emoluments of his employment, or by accepting any part of the fees, profits or gains of a lawyer, chartered accountant, broker or agent engaged by his employer. The profession's fee-sharing discipline follows the member into service — kickbacks on either side of an employer's engagements are the mischief.

Every tax audit report carries Form 3CD, the statement of particulars; what varies is its cover. Form 3CA is used where the accounts are already audited under any other law — a company under the Companies Act — and it references that statutory audit; Form 3CB is used where no other audit exists, and there the tax auditor himself expresses the true and fair opinion on the accounts. Picking 3CB for a company duplicates an opinion someone else owns.

CARO's second clause covers inventory and borrowings against it: whether physical verification of inventory was conducted at reasonable intervals with material discrepancies dealt with in the books — and, where working capital limits above five crore rupees are sanctioned against current assets, whether the quarterly returns filed with the banks agree with the books of account, with disagreements detailed. Statements to bankers and statements to shareholders must be the same statements.

Performance audit examines the three Es — economy (spending less for the same inputs), efficiency (getting more output per input), and effectiveness (achieving the intended outcome) — of a programme or entity, against criteria agreed or derived, reporting findings and recommendations rather than an opinion. It differs from propriety audit's transaction-level prudence test: performance audit judges the scheme, not the voucher.

citation.ref: Ch. Audit of Public Sector Undertakings

concepts.statement: The statutory auditor's review of a listed company's quarterly results runs under SRE 2410: inquiry of finance personnel and analytical procedures, sized for limited assurance, concluding in negative form. It is not a small audit — no control testing, no third-party confirmations by default — but the auditor who becomes aware of a possible material misstatement must extend procedures until the doubt resolves; the lighter vehicle carries no licence to drive past red flags.

concepts.subsection: Code of Ethics — Responding to NOCLAR
concepts.statement: On becoming aware of non-compliance or suspected non-compliance with laws and regulations at a client, the member's response runs in sequence: understand the matter, raise it with the appropriate level of management and those charged with governance, urge rectification and disclosure, then judge whether further action — up to withdrawal or disclosure to an authority — is needed in the public interest. Confidentiality does not bar a disclosure the framework calls for; walking away silently is the response the framework rejects.

citation.ref: Responding to Non-Compliance with Laws and Regulations

concepts.statement: Where a company has made investments in, given guarantees or security for, or granted loans or advances in the nature of loans to any parties, CARO asks: the amounts involved (with related-party loans separately shown), whether the terms are prejudicial to the company's interests, whether repayment schedules exist and repayments are regular, overdue amounts beyond ninety days and the steps taken, whether loans were renewed or fresh loans settled old ones, and loans repayable on demand or without terms — again with the related-party share disclosed.

concepts.subsection: Section 54 — Capital gains on residential property
concepts.statement: Section 54 exempts long-term capital gains on the transfer of a residential house only when the gain is reinvested in a residential house in India — purchased within one year before or two years after the transfer, or constructed within three years. Reinvestment in commercial property earns no exemption.

Tax audit applies to a business at turnover above ₹1 crore, but the limit rises to ₹10 crore where cash receipts and cash payments each stay within 5 per cent of the respective totals. For a profession the limit is gross receipts above ₹50 lakh.

A domestic company that opts for section 115BAA pays tax at the concessional rate, must give up the specified deductions and incentives, and is outside MAT entirely — book profit tax does not apply to it at all.

A company files its return by 31 October of the assessment year. Where it must furnish a transfer pricing report under section 92E, the due date extends to 30 November. The 31 July date belongs to persons with no audit requirement.

Long-term capital gains on listed equity shares where STT is paid are taxed under section 112A above an annual exemption threshold, without indexation. The rate and threshold are Finance Act figures and move; the structure — exemption slab, no indexation, STT condition — is the stable part.

An eligible resident individual, HUF or firm with business turnover within the limit may declare profit at 8 per cent of turnover — 6 per cent for amounts received through banking channels — and skip books and tax audit. Companies and LLPs are outside the scheme, as are commission, agency and section 44AE transport businesses.

concepts.subsection: Sections 72 and 80 — Carry forward of losses
concepts.statement: A business loss carries forward for eight assessment years, but only if the return of the loss year was filed by its due date — section 80 makes the timely return the price of the carry forward. Unabsorbed depreciation lives under section 32(2) instead, needs no timely return, and has no eight-year limit.

Money received without consideration is taxable as other-sources income if the aggregate from all persons in the year exceeds fifty thousand rupees — and then the whole amount is taxed, not the excess. Gifts from relatives as defined, and on the occasion of the individual's marriage, stay outside regardless of size.

A resident individual or firm in a specified profession with gross receipts within the limit may declare 50 per cent of receipts as income. The enhanced limit applies where cash receipts stay within 5 per cent. Declaring less than 50 per cent while over the basic exemption brings books and audit.

concepts.subsection: Section 194-IA — TDS on purchase of property
concepts.statement: A buyer of immovable property, other than rural agricultural land, deducts tax at 1 per cent of the consideration where consideration or stamp duty value is fifty lakh rupees or more — and then on the whole amount, not the excess. The buyer needs no TAN; the deduction rides on the buyer's PAN.

An individual is resident if present in India for 182 days in the year, or 60 days in the year plus 365 across the four preceding years. The 60-day limb stretches to 182 for a citizen leaving for employment or as crew, and to 120 for a visiting citizen or person of Indian origin whose Indian income exceeds fifteen lakh rupees.

A minor child's income is clubbed with the income of the parent whose total income is higher, with an exemption of fifteen hundred rupees per child. Income from the minor's own manual work or from activity involving the minor's skill and talent stays with the minor.

Loss under house property can be set off against other heads only up to two lakh rupees in a year; the balance carries forward for eight years, and then only against house property income. The interest deduction itself may be larger — the cap bites at set-off, not at computation.

concepts.subsection: Section 43B(h) — Payments to micro and small enterprises
concepts.statement: Sums payable to micro and small enterprises are deductible only in the year of actual payment when paid beyond the time section 15 of the MSMED Act allows — and the usual escape of paying before the return's due date does not apply to this clause. Medium enterprises are outside it.

concepts.subsection: Section 50C — Stamp duty value on transfer of land or building
concepts.statement: Where land or a building sells below its stamp duty value, the stamp value is deemed the consideration for capital gains — but only when it exceeds one hundred and ten per cent of the actual consideration; within that tolerance the actual price stands. The seller can also ask for a valuation officer's reference where the stamp value is contested.

Where tax deductible on a payment to a resident is not deducted, or not deposited by the return's due date, thirty per cent of the expense is disallowed — not the whole of it — and the thirty per cent comes back as a deduction in the year the tax is finally paid.

The 54EC exemption is only for long-term capital gains from land or a building or both, only up to fifty lakh rupees in a financial year, and only where the specified bonds are bought within six months of transfer. The bonds lock in for five years, and taking a loan against them counts as cashing out.

concepts.subsection: Section 79 — Carry forward on change in shareholding
concepts.statement: A closely held company loses its carried-forward losses if, on the last day of the year the loss is set off, shares carrying at least fifty-one per cent of voting power are not held by the persons who held them on the last day of the loss year. Eligible start-ups get a softer test — continuity of all original shareholders, or the seven-year window. Unabsorbed depreciation is outside section 79 entirely.

concepts.subsection: Section 90(4) — Treaty relief and the TRC
concepts.statement: A non-resident claiming treaty benefit must hold a tax residency certificate from its home government; without it the treaty door does not open. The Act also lets the taxpayer choose whichever is more beneficial — treaty or domestic law — provision by provision, and a treaty can never be used to make the position worse than the Act.

An unexplained credit in the books is taxed as income unless the taxpayer explains its nature and source to the officer's satisfaction; for share capital in a closely held company, the source of the source — the resident investor's own funds — must be explained too. Income taxed this way falls under section 115BBE: a sixty per cent rate plus surcharge, with no deductions, allowances, or set-off of losses against it.

concepts.subsection: Section 64(1)(iv) — Income from assets transferred to spouse
concepts.statement: Income from an asset transferred to a spouse without adequate consideration is clubbed with the transferor's income. The clubbing follows the transferred asset's income, not income earned on that income — reinvested earnings belong to the spouse. A transfer before the marriage, or for adequate consideration, or under an agreement to live apart, escapes.

An assessee owning not more than ten goods carriages at any time in the year may declare presumptive income: for a heavy goods vehicle (over 12MT gross weight), one thousand rupees per ton of gross vehicle weight per month or part; for others, seven thousand five hundred per vehicle per month or part. Ownership months count, idle or running; declaring lower than the presumption invites books and audit.

GAAR strikes an arrangement whose main purpose is a tax benefit and which carries a tainted element — non-arm's-length dealings, misuse of the Act, lack of commercial substance, or means not ordinarily employed for bona fide purposes. Both limbs must be satisfied; a tax benefit alone is legitimate planning. The rules spare arrangements whose aggregate tax benefit is within three crore rupees.

concepts.subsection: Transfer pricing — Arm's length price methods
concepts.statement: The arm's length price of an international transaction between associated enterprises is determined by the most appropriate of the prescribed methods — comparable uncontrolled price, resale price, cost plus, profit split, transactional net margin, or other prescribed method. No hierarchy ranks them; suitability to the transaction, functions and available data picks the method, and CUP prevails only when true comparables exist.

A company not under the concessional regimes pays the higher of tax on total income and fifteen per cent of book profit — the audited profit adjusted by the section's own list of additions and deletions. Excess MAT paid becomes credit, carried forward to set against regular tax for up to fifteen years. Companies opting into section 115BAA leave MAT, and MAT credit, behind.

Under-reported income draws a penalty of fifty per cent of the tax on it; where the under-reporting flows from misreporting — misrepresentation of facts, false entries, unrecorded investments, claims without evidence — the penalty is two hundred per cent. A bona fide explanation with disclosed material facts takes an addition out of under-reporting altogether; immunity under section 270AA needs tax and interest paid and no appeal, and never covers misreporting.

concepts.subsection: Section 263 — Revision of orders prejudicial to revenue
concepts.statement: The Commissioner may revise an assessment only where it is both erroneous and prejudicial to the revenue's interests — two conditions, cumulative. An officer's view that is a possible view after real enquiry is not erroneous merely because the Commissioner prefers another; no enquiry where enquiry was called for is the classic error. The window is two years from the end of the financial year of the order.

Interest paid to a non-resident associated enterprise beyond one crore rupees is deductible only up to thirty per cent of EBITDA; the excess carries forward up to eight years. The section reaches loans guaranteed by the associated enterprise too, and spares banks and insurers. It caps deduction, not the interest's character — TDS and the lender's taxation run unaffected.

concepts.subsection: Section 9 — Business connection and significant economic presence
concepts.statement: A non-resident's income is deemed to accrue in India through a business connection — which since 2018 includes an agent habitually playing the principal role in concluding contracts, and since the SEP amendment, a significant economic presence built on transactions or user engagement in India without any physical presence. Treaty definitions of permanent establishment still override for treaty residents, which keeps SEP's bite mainly on non-treaty cases.

A registered trust's income is exempt to the extent applied to charitable purposes in India, with at least eighty-five per cent to be applied in the year — fifteen per cent may be accumulated freely. Falling short, the trust may accumulate for up to five years for a specific purpose by filing the prescribed statement, or treat income received late as applied when actually spent. Application now counts on payment, not accrual.

A slump sale transfers an undertaking as a going concern for a lump sum without itemised values; capital gain is the deemed consideration — the fair market value computed under the rules — less the undertaking's net worth as cost of acquisition, with net worth computed on the prescribed basis, ignoring revaluations. An undertaking held over thirty-six months yields long-term gain even though depreciable assets ride inside it.

A person providing any benefit or perquisite arising from business or profession — foreign trips for dealers, gifted cars, sponsored gadgets, waived debts — deducts ten per cent of its value, where the aggregate to a recipient exceeds twenty thousand rupees in the year. The deduction applies whether the benefit is in cash or kind or partly both, and for benefits wholly in kind the provider must ensure tax is paid before releasing them.

In-house scientific research related to the business earns deduction of both revenue and capital expenditure — land excluded — in the year incurred; pre-commencement research expenditure of the three prior years is deductible in the year business begins. The weighted deductions of the past have sunset to one hundred per cent, and contributions to approved institutions ride their own approval-dependent limbs.

concepts.subsection: Corporate residence — place of effective management
concepts.statement: A foreign company is resident in India if its place of effective management — where key management and commercial decisions necessary for the business as a whole are in substance made — is in India that year. Board meetings held abroad do not settle it when the board merely ratifies decisions taken in India; conversely, active regional headquarters abroad making the decisions keep POEM outside. The test is substance over minutes.

The Commissioner (Appeals) may confirm, reduce, enhance or annul an assessment — the power to enhance makes the first appeal a two-edged forum, exercisable only after a reasonable opportunity to show cause. What the first appellate authority lacks is the power to set aside and remand the assessment for a fresh run; the appeal must be decided, point by point.

For buy-backs on or after 1 October 2024, the company-level buy-back tax is gone: the entire consideration a shareholder receives is deemed a dividend under section 2(22)(f), taxable at slab rates with no deduction for cost, and subject to dividend TDS. The shares' cost is not lost — the transfer is computed with consideration deemed nil, manufacturing a capital loss that sets off and carries forward against capital gains only.

A loan or advance by a closely held company to a shareholder holding ten per cent or more of voting power — or to a concern in which such a shareholder is substantially interested — is deemed a dividend to the extent of the company's accumulated profits. Repayment later does not undo the deeming; loans in the ordinary course of a money-lending business and certain set-offs escape it.

Speculation loss sets off only against speculation profit, and carries forward just four years. A speculative transaction settles otherwise than by actual delivery — but eligible exchange-traded derivatives are excluded from the definition, while the Explanation to section 73 deems a company's share-trading business speculative unless the company falls in the carved-out categories. Delivery-based investing and F&O thus sit outside; a company churning shares as a business sits inside.

Agricultural income is exempt, but for individuals with net agricultural income above five thousand rupees and other income above the basic exemption, it enters the rate machinery: tax is computed on the aggregate, then reduced by tax on agricultural income plus the exemption limit. The farm income is never taxed itself — it pushes the other income into higher slabs. Companies and firms, taxed at flat rates, are outside the scheme.

citation.ref: Section 10(1) with Finance Act rate schedule

concepts.statement: Certain sums deduct only when actually paid, whatever the books accrue: taxes, duties and cesses, employer contributions to funds, bonus and commission to employees, interest to banks and financial institutions, and leave encashment among them. Payment by the return's due date saves the year's deduction; converting unpaid interest into a fresh loan is expressly not payment, and the deduction waits for the converted loan's actual repayment.

concepts.subsection: Section 194Q — TDS on purchase of goods
concepts.statement: A buyer whose turnover exceeded ten crore rupees in the preceding year deducts tax at 0.1 per cent on purchases from a resident seller beyond fifty lakh rupees in the year, deducting on the excess. The mirror-image seller-side TCS on goods stood omitted from 1 April 2025, ending the old overlap where the buyer's TDS took precedence — the buyer's obligation now stands alone. Failure invites the thirty per cent disallowance for TDS defaults.

citation.ref: Section 194Q (TCS on goods omitted w.e.f. 1 April 2025)

concepts.subsection: Section 54F — Investment of any LTCG in a house
concepts.statement: Long-term gain on any capital asset other than a residential house is exempt where the net consideration — not merely the gain — is invested in one residential house in India, proportionately where investment falls short, capped at ten crore rupees of investment. The gates: not owning more than one other residential house on the transfer date, and no second house purchase within the lock-in windows. Section 54, by contrast, covers house-to-house and asks only the gain to be reinvested.

An updated return may be filed within forty-eight months of the assessment year's end — the window doubled by the Finance Act 2025 — on payment of additional tax that climbs with delay: twenty-five per cent of tax and interest in the first twelve months, fifty in the next, sixty in the third year, seventy in the fourth. It can only add to the tax take: no updated return may declare a loss, shrink the liability, or enlarge a refund.

A firm deducts working partners' remuneration only if the deed authorises it, and within the ceiling: on the first six lakh rupees of book profit (or a loss), the higher of three lakh rupees or ninety per cent of that slice; on the balance, sixty per cent — limits doubled by the Finance Act 2024 from assessment year 2025-26. Interest to partners caps at twelve per cent simple. From April 2025, section 194T adds ten per cent TDS on partner payments above twenty thousand rupees a year.

A bad debt deducts in the year it is written off in the books — since 1989 the write-off itself is enough, and the assessee need not prove the debt actually became irrecoverable that year. The debt must have been counted in income earlier (or be money lent in a lending business). Recovery of an allowed bad debt is taxed when received, and a successor cannot claim the predecessor's debtor.

concepts.subsection: ICDS — Income computation and disclosure standards
concepts.statement: The ten notified ICDS govern computation of business income and other sources for taxpayers following mercantile accounting — they change the tax computation, never the books. Where ICDS diverges from accounting standards, ICDS wins for tax; where ICDS conflicts with the Act itself, the Act prevails. Familiar divergences: expected losses on construction contracts are not anticipated, marked-to-market losses are generally ignored, and retention money follows the ICDS timing.

Donations for which a charitable trust maintains no record of the donor's name and address are taxed at thirty per cent — after a cushion of the higher of one lakh rupees or five per cent of total donations. Wholly religious institutions are outside the section entirely; mixed religious-charitable ones are caught only for donations directed to their educational or medical wings. The hundi at a temple and the box at a hospital answer to different rules.

Specified preliminary expenses — feasibility and project reports, engineering services, legal charges for agreements, and for companies the incorporation and issue expenses — amortise in five equal annual instalments from commencement or extension. The pool is capped at five per cent of the cost of the project (companies may take five per cent of capital employed instead); spending beyond the cap earns no deduction at all under the section.

Accepting an audit previously held by another chartered accountant without first communicating with him in writing is professional misconduct. The duty is to communicate — the outgoing auditor's permission or no-objection is not required, and the purpose is to learn whether the change hides something the incoming auditor should weigh.

Disclosing information acquired in the course of a professional engagement to anyone other than the client, without the client's consent, is professional misconduct — unless law requires the disclosure. Legal compulsion and client consent are the only two doors out of the duty.

Expressing an opinion on the financial statements of any business in which the member, his firm, or a partner in his firm has a substantial interest is professional misconduct. The clause reaches the firm and the partners, not only the signing member, and no disclosure cures it — the opinion itself is barred.

Failing to exercise due diligence, or being grossly negligent in the conduct of professional duties, is professional misconduct. The clause needs no dishonesty and no client loss — signing what was never examined is the classic case.

A chartered accountant in practice may not engage in any business or occupation other than the profession unless the Council permits it. The clause's own proviso allows a directorship simpliciter — an ordinary board seat without managing or whole-time office — unless the member or a partner is interested in the company as its auditor. General and specific permissions of the Council carve the remaining space.

Failing to keep a client's moneys — other than fees or money meant to be spent — in a separate banking account, or failing to use such moneys for their intended purpose within a reasonable time, is professional misconduct. The office account is for the firm's money; the client account is for the client's, and mixing them is the offence regardless of eventual repayment.

Advertising professional attainments or services, or using any designation other than chartered accountant on professional documents, cards or sign boards, is misconduct — a recognised university degree or a title indicating membership of an institute may be used. The Council's guidelines carve narrow permissions — write-ups within prescribed norms, websites on a pull basis — but self-praise pushed at the public stays barred.

Paying or allowing any share, commission or brokerage out of professional fees to anyone other than a member of the Institute, a partner, a retired partner, a deceased partner's legal representative, or a member of a permitted other professional body is misconduct. The clause polices the outflow of fees; referral commissions to clients, agents or relatives all fall on the wrong side.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 115 — Costs to obtain and fulfil a contract
concepts.statement: The incremental costs of obtaining a contract are recognised as an asset if the entity expects to recover them, with a practical expedient to expense them if the amortisation period is one year or less. Costs to fulfil a contract that are not within another Standard's scope are capitalised only if they relate directly to an identified contract, generate or enhance resources used to satisfy performance obligations, and are expected to be recovered.

Hedge accounting is available only where the hedging relationship consists solely of eligible hedging instruments and eligible hedged items, there is formal designation and documentation at inception of the risk management objective and strategy, and the relationship meets the effectiveness requirements — an economic relationship between the hedged item and the hedging instrument, credit risk not dominating the value changes, and a hedge ratio consistent with actual risk management.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 109 — Derecognition of financial assets
concepts.statement: A financial asset is derecognised when the contractual rights to its cash flows expire, or when it is transferred and that transfer qualifies for derecognition — which turns on evaluating the extent to which the risks and rewards of ownership are retained. Substantially transferring risks and rewards derecognises the asset; substantially retaining them keeps it recognised in full, with a financial liability for the consideration received; only when neither is clear does the entity move on to a control test.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 12 — Deferred tax in a business combination
concepts.statement: Fair value adjustments to identifiable assets and liabilities recognised on a business combination create temporary differences whenever the tax base does not move to match, and the resulting deferred tax asset or liability is recognised as part of the acquisition accounting — increasing or decreasing goodwill or the bargain purchase gain. The one carve-out is goodwill itself — no deferred tax liability is recognised on its initial recognition, because that would only inflate goodwill further.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 21 — Net investment in a foreign operation
concepts.statement: Exchange differences on a monetary item that in substance forms part of an entity's net investment in a foreign operation are recognised in profit or loss in the separate or individual financial statements of the entity concerned, but in the financial statements that include the foreign operation — such as the group's consolidated statements — those exchange differences go to other comprehensive income and are reclassified to profit or loss only on disposal of the net investment.

In a sale and leaseback, the seller-lessee applies the Ind AS 115 requirements for identifying when a performance obligation is satisfied to judge whether the transfer is a sale. If it is, the seller-lessee measures the right-of-use asset retained at the proportion of the previous carrying amount relating to the rights retained, and recognises only the gain or loss relating to the rights transferred to the buyer-lessor — not the full gain on the asset. If the transfer fails the sale test, both parties account for it as a financing.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 36 — Timing of the goodwill impairment test
concepts.statement: A cash-generating unit to which goodwill has been allocated is tested for impairment at least annually, and the test may be performed at any time during the annual period provided it is performed at the same time every year; different units may be tested at different times. If some or all of the goodwill allocated to a unit was acquired in a business combination during the current period, that unit is tested before the end of the current annual period — the entity cannot wait for next year's cycle.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 33 — Diluted EPS and antidilution
concepts.statement: Diluted EPS adjusts profit and the weighted average number of shares for the effect of all dilutive potential equity shares, but a potential equity share that would increase EPS (or reduce a loss per share) is antidilutive and is excluded from the diluted EPS computation. Each issue or series of potential equity shares is tested for dilutive or antidilutive effect separately, not in aggregate.

A contingent asset is never recognised, because that could bring in income that may never be realised — but it is disclosed when an inflow of economic benefits is probable. Once realisation becomes virtually certain, the asset is no longer contingent and is recognised, together with the related income, in the period the change occurs.

For a cash-settled share-based payment, the entity measures the goods or services received and the liability incurred at the fair value of the liability, and remeasures that fair value at the end of every reporting period and at settlement, with all changes recognised in profit or loss. Unlike an equity-settled award, the amount charged is never frozen at grant date — it moves with the liability's fair value until the award is paid.

Management assesses the entity's ability to continue as a going concern, looking at least twelve months from the reporting date, and prepares the financial statements on that basis unless it intends to liquidate or cease trading or has no realistic alternative. Where management identifies material uncertainties that cast significant doubt on that ability, those uncertainties are disclosed — disclosure, not abandonment of the going concern basis, is the standard's response short of an actual intention to liquidate.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 8 — Correction of prior period errors
concepts.statement: A material prior period error is corrected retrospectively in the first financial statements approved after its discovery, by restating the comparative amounts for the period the error occurred, or restating opening balances if the error predates the earliest period presented. The correction bypasses profit or loss for the period of discovery — it adjusts the periods actually affected, not the current period's result.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 115 — Revenue from Contracts with Customers
concepts.statement: Revenue is recognised when (or as) a performance obligation is satisfied by transferring control of the promised good or service to the customer. Transfer of control, not transfer of risks and rewards, is the recognition trigger.
Inventories of items that are not ordinarily interchangeable are costed by specific identification. For the rest, FIFO or weighted average is used. LIFO is not permitted.

An investor controls an investee only when it has all three elements together — power over the investee, exposure or rights to variable returns, and the ability to use its power to affect those returns. Control does not require a majority shareholding.

Loss allowances are measured on an expected credit loss basis, recognised from initial recognition without waiting for a default. For trade receivables the simplified approach applies, and the allowance is always lifetime expected credit losses.

Under the Indian carve-out, a gain on a bargain purchase is recognised in other comprehensive income and accumulated in capital reserve, not in profit or loss — unlike IFRS 3, which takes it to profit or loss.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 115 — Revenue from Contracts with Customers
concepts.statement: A performance obligation is satisfied over time only when one of three criteria is met — the customer consumes the benefit as the entity performs, the customer controls the asset as it is created, or the asset has no alternative use and the entity has an enforceable right to payment for performance to date. Otherwise control passes at a point in time.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 37 — Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets
concepts.statement: A provision is recognised only when all three conditions hold — a present obligation, legal or constructive, from a past event; a probable outflow of resources; and a reliable estimate. For a restructuring, the obligating event is announcing the plan to those affected or beginning to implement it, never the board decision alone.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 16 — Property, Plant and Equipment
concepts.statement: The cost of a major inspection or overhaul that is a condition of continuing to operate an asset is capitalised into the asset's carrying amount when incurred, and any remaining carrying amount of the previous inspection is derecognised — even if the previous inspection's cost was never separately identified.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 21 — The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates
concepts.statement: At each reporting date, foreign currency monetary items are translated at the closing rate, with exchange differences to profit or loss. Non-monetary items carried at historical cost stay at the transaction-date rate. Whether an item is money fixes which rate it gets.

Internally generated goodwill is never recognised as an asset, and internally generated brands, mastheads, customer lists and similar items are barred with it. Development costs are the exception, capitalised only from the day all six conditions are demonstrated; research is always expensed.

An operating segment is separately reportable if it crosses ten per cent of combined revenue (internal plus external), of the greater of combined profits or combined losses, or of combined assets — and reportable segments must together cover seventy-five per cent of external revenue, adding segments until they do.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 1 — Presentation of Financial Statements
concepts.statement: A liability is current when the entity lacks, at the reporting date, the right to defer settlement for at least twelve months. A covenant breached by the year end makes the loan payable on demand and therefore current — unless the lender agreed, on or before the reporting date, not to demand payment; a waiver arriving after the year end comes too late to change the classification.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 7 — Statement of Cash Flows
concepts.statement: Under the Indian carve-out, an entity other than a financial institution classifies interest paid as a financing cash flow and interest and dividends received as investing — the options IFRS offers are removed. A bank classifies all of them as operating, because lending is its business.

A lessee recognises a right-of-use asset and a lease liability for every lease, with two elections out — leases of twelve months or less with no purchase option, and leases of low-value assets. The exemptions are elections about recognition, not about whether the contract is a lease.

An asset is impaired when its carrying amount exceeds its recoverable amount, and recoverable amount is the higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use. Higher — the entity keeps the better of selling and using, so either measure alone can clear the asset of impairment.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 10 — Events after the Reporting Period
concepts.statement: An event after the reporting period adjusts the financial statements only when it evidences a condition that existed at the reporting date; a condition that arose afterwards is disclosed, not adjusted. Dividends declared after the reporting period are the standard's own worked example — no liability at the reporting date, however certain the declaration.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 105 — Non-current Assets Held for Sale
concepts.statement: Held-for-sale classification needs the asset available for immediate sale in its present condition and the sale highly probable — management committed to a plan, an active programme to find a buyer, active marketing at a reasonable price, and completion expected within a year. Once classified, the asset is measured at the lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell, and depreciation stops.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 8 — Policies, Estimates and Errors
concepts.statement: A change in accounting policy is applied retrospectively, restating comparatives as if the new policy had always applied; a change in accounting estimate is recognised prospectively, in the period of change and the future. Where the two are hard to tell apart, the standard itself says treat the change as an estimate. Depreciation method and useful life are estimates; measurement basis is policy.

Borrowing costs directly attributable to acquiring, constructing or producing a qualifying asset — one that necessarily takes a substantial period to get ready for its intended use or sale — are capitalised as part of the asset's cost; all other borrowing costs are expensed. Capitalisation is suspended during extended periods when active development pauses, and ends when the asset is substantially ready.

Ind AS 40 permits only the cost model for investment property — the Indian carve-out removed IAS 40's fair value model. Fair value is still measured and disclosed in the notes, but the balance sheet carries cost less depreciation and impairment. Property held to earn rentals or for capital appreciation, not for use in production or administration, is what the standard covers.

citation.ref: measurement after recognition (cost model; fair value model not permitted)

concepts.statement: The fair value hierarchy ranks inputs, not techniques: Level 1 is unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical items; Level 2 is other observable inputs — quoted prices for similar items, or corroborated market data; Level 3 is unobservable inputs. A measurement sits at the lowest level of any input significant to it, and Level 1 prices are used unadjusted where available.

For equity-settled awards to employees, the expense is measured at the fair value of the equity instruments at grant date — and that value is never remeasured, however the share price moves. What does move is the number of awards expected to vest under service and non-market conditions, trued up each period until vesting. Market conditions are priced into grant-date value once and never trued up.

Defined benefit cost splits three ways: service cost and net interest go to profit or loss; remeasurements — actuarial gains and losses, and the return on plan assets beyond the amount already in net interest — go to other comprehensive income, and once there they are never reclassified to profit or loss. The split keeps the operating result clear of actuarial volatility without hiding it.

Twenty per cent or more of voting power presumes significant influence — the power to participate in financial and operating policy decisions — and less than twenty presumes its absence; both presumptions yield to clear demonstration otherwise. Board representation, policy participation, material transactions, interchange of personnel or essential technical dependence can evidence influence below the line. An associate is equity accounted, not consolidated.

A deferred tax asset on unused tax losses is recognised only to the extent future taxable profit is probable — and a history of recent losses is itself evidence against that. A loss-making entity records the asset only to the extent of taxable temporary differences or convincing other evidence of future profit, such as a firm order book from a cause that has demonstrably ended.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 109 — Classification of financial assets
concepts.statement: A financial asset is carried at amortised cost only when both tests pass: the business model is to hold and collect contractual cash flows, and those cash flows are solely payments of principal and interest. Held-to-collect with equity-linked returns fails the second; plain-interest bonds bought for trading fail the first. Failures land in fair value categories.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 103 — Non-controlling interest at acquisition
concepts.statement: For each business combination, the acquirer measures qualifying non-controlling interest at either full fair value or the proportionate share of the acquiree's identifiable net assets — a choice made combination by combination, not as a standing policy. The choice sets goodwill: fair value NCI produces full goodwill including the minority's share; the proportionate route recognises only the acquirer's goodwill.

Lessors still classify: a lease that transfers substantially all the risks and rewards of ownership is a finance lease — derecognise the asset, recognise a receivable; otherwise it is an operating lease — keep the asset, book income over the term. Indicators include ownership transfer, a bargain purchase option, the term covering the major part of economic life, and present value of payments amounting to substantially all the fair value. Lessee accounting became single-model; lessor accounting did not.

An instrument is classified by substance against the definitions, not by its legal name: a contractual obligation to deliver cash — mandatory redemption, compulsory dividends — makes a financial liability, however the instrument is titled. Preference shares redeemable at the holder's option or on a fixed date are debt; pure discretion over both dividends and redemption keeps an instrument in equity. Classification happens once, at issue.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 33 — EPS and bonus issues
concepts.statement: A bonus issue, split or similar event changes the share count without changing resources, so EPS treats the new count as if it had existed from the beginning of the earliest period presented — restating the comparative EPS too. A fresh issue for cash, by contrast, enters the weighted average only from its date, because new resources arrived then.

Key management personnel compensation is disclosed in total and by category — short-term, post-employment, other long-term, termination, share-based. Related party disclosure is about relationships and transactions, not approval: arm's length terms may be claimed only if they can be substantiated, and a government-related entity gets a partial exemption for dealings with its government and its sister entities, disclosing the nature and extent instead of every transaction.

Interim statements apply the same accounting policies as the annual ones — a quarter is not a licence for different measurement — and reporting frequency must not change the annual result: measurements run year-to-date, so a third-quarter estimate correction adjusts the year-to-date figures rather than fabricating a standalone quarter. Costs that fail asset definitions at year-end fail them equally at a quarter's end.

A contract whose unavoidable costs of fulfilment exceed the benefits expected under it is onerous, and the present obligation is provided for at once — the unavoidable cost being the lower of the cost of fulfilling and the penalty of exiting. Routine cancellable purchase orders create no obligation, and expected future operating losses of the business generally are never provided for; the onerous contract is the exception because the loss is contracted, not merely forecast.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 111 — Joint operations and joint ventures
concepts.statement: Joint control is contractually agreed sharing of control where the relevant decisions need unanimous consent. The arrangement's type decides the accounting: joint operators have rights to the assets and obligations for the liabilities and record their share of each, line by line; joint venturers have rights only to the net assets and equity-account the investment. Structure through a separate vehicle starts, not ends, the classification.

A government grant is recognised only when there is reasonable assurance the entity will comply with its conditions and the grant will be received. Since the 2018 amendment, a grant related to an asset may be presented either as deferred income released over the asset's life, or by deducting it from the asset's carrying amount — the pre-2018 Indian text had removed the deduction option, and stale materials still teach that removal.

A first-time adopter may elect deemed cost for property, plant and equipment at the transition date: fair value at that date, or the previous GAAP carrying amount where eligible — instead of rebuilding depreciated cost as if Ind AS had always applied. The elections are optional exemptions from full retrospective application; the general rule remains retrospective, and mandatory exceptions forbid hindsight in estimates.

citation.ref: deemed cost exemption for PPE at transition

concepts.statement: An entity is a principal when it controls the promised good or service before transfer to the customer, reporting gross revenue; an agent arranges for another to provide it, reporting only its fee or commission. Momentary legal title on the way through does not make a principal; inventory risk, primary responsibility for fulfilment and discretion in setting prices indicate control. The revenue difference is presentation, not profit.

When a parent loses control of a subsidiary it derecognises the subsidiary's assets, liabilities and NCI, recognises the consideration received, and measures any retained interest at fair value at that date — that fair value becomes the cost of the new associate or investment. The gain or loss in profit or loss thus includes a remeasurement of the stake kept, not only the stake sold; control is an all-or-nothing line.

Under the revaluation model an upward revaluation goes to other comprehensive income and accumulates in equity as revaluation surplus — except to the extent it reverses a decrease earlier charged to profit or loss. A downward revaluation charges profit or loss — except to the extent a surplus for that same asset exists to absorb it. The surplus never passes through profit or loss: on disposal it transfers directly to retained earnings.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 2 — NRV and the raw materials exception
concepts.statement: Inventories are carried at the lower of cost and net realisable value, item by item — but raw materials are not written down below cost while the finished products they will enter are expected to sell at or above cost. Only when the materials' price decline signals that the finished product's cost exceeds its NRV do the materials write down, with replacement cost as their best available measure.

Biological assets are measured at each reporting date at fair value less costs to sell, with changes through profit or loss — cost models yield to the market's verdict on living, growing assets. Bearer plants — the tea bush, not the tea leaf — are carved out to Ind AS 16 as plant-like assets, while the produce growing on them stays in Ind AS 41 until harvest, when it moves to Ind AS 2 at its harvest-date fair value as deemed cost.

concepts.subsection: Schedule III — Mandated ratios and disclosures
concepts.statement: Division II of Schedule III requires eleven named ratios in the notes — current ratio, debt-equity, debt service coverage, return on equity, inventory and receivables and payables turnover, net capital turnover, net profit, return on capital employed, return on investment — with the elements of each computation and an explanation wherever a ratio moved more than twenty-five per cent from the prior year. The amendments also demand disclosure of benami proceedings, undisclosed income surrendered, and crypto holdings.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 28 — Sharing an associate's losses
concepts.statement: Equity accounting absorbs an associate's losses only down to zero: once the investor's share of losses equals its interest — the equity-method carrying amount plus long-term interests that are in substance part of the net investment — recognition of further losses stops, resuming only after future profits rebuild the base. Losses beyond zero are provided only where the investor has legal or constructive obligations or made payments for the associate.

Variable consideration — bonuses, penalties, volume rebates, royalties — enters the transaction price only to the extent it is highly probable that a significant reversal of cumulative revenue will not occur when the uncertainty resolves. Estimation uses the expected value or the most likely amount, whichever predicts better; the constraint then trims the estimate. Booking the hopeful number and reversing later is the pattern the rule exists to stop.

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 7 — Cash and cash equivalents
concepts.statement: Cash equivalents are short-term, highly liquid investments readily convertible to known amounts of cash with insignificant risk of value change — normally maturing within about three months of acquisition. Equity investments are excluded save in-substance equivalents. Bank overdrafts repayable on demand that form an integral part of cash management join cash and cash equivalents, turning the statement's bottom line negative-capable.

Consolidation combines like items line by line, eliminates the parent's investment against its share of each subsidiary's equity, and eliminates intragroup balances, transactions and unrealised profits in full — not merely the parent's share. The group reports as one economic entity under uniform accounting policies for like transactions, restating a subsidiary's numbers where its policies differ.

Quorum for a board meeting is the higher of one-third of the total strength of directors (any fraction rounded up) or two directors. A director interested in an item under section 184(2) is left out of the count for that item, and telephonic assent from a director not participating by the prescribed video-conferencing means does not count as presence. Absent quorum, the meeting stands automatically adjourned to the same day the following week, same time and place, unless the articles say otherwise.

Every company holds at least four board meetings a year, with the gap between two consecutive meetings never exceeding one hundred and twenty days, and the first meeting within thirty days of incorporation. A one person company, small company, dormant company or private start-up needs only one meeting in each half of the calendar year, with a minimum gap of ninety days between the two — a relaxation, not the general rule.

concepts.subsection: Board powers needing shareholder approval — section 180
concepts.statement: The board cannot, by its own resolution, sell, lease or otherwise dispose of the whole or substantially the whole of an undertaking, or borrow beyond the aggregate of paid-up capital, free reserves and securities premium (ordinary-course temporary bank loans excepted) — both need a special resolution of the shareholders first, obtained before the act, not disclosed to them after it.

Independent directors are never liable to retire by rotation. Of the remaining directors of a public company, at least two-thirds must be liable to rotation, of which one-third (or the number nearest to one-third) retires at every annual general meeting, the director longest in office retiring first and being eligible for reappointment. Articles cannot exempt directors from rotation below this statutory floor.
